articles.title: Single people who pursue novel activities report better psychological health, study finds
articles.summary: Being single offers a unique chance for personal growth. A recent psychology study suggests that single adults who view their relationship status as an opportunity to try new things experience greater daily well-being and less anxiety.

articles.title: Social anxiety and depression appear to change the way we process feedback
articles.summary: A new study reveals how social anxiety and depression distort the way people update their self-beliefs in response to feedback. While social anxiety amplifies negative judgments about competence, depression makes it difficult to accept positive feedback entirely.

articles.title: A Long-Run Persistence Theory for AI Systems under the Redundancy-Adjusted Artificial Age Score (AAS)
articles.summary: arXiv:2608.04012v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Artificial intelligence systems are increasingly expected to operate over repeated cycles of interaction, adaptation, and update rather than through isolated one-shot outputs. This raises a fundamental theoretical question: can an AI system persist indefinitely without incurring unbounded structural aging? This paper develops a long-run persistence framework for AI systems based on the redundancy-adjusted Artificial Age Score (AAS). The model extends AAS from a static evaluative measure into a cycle-level functional that generates an age sequence

articles.title: The LLM Proposes, the Executive Disposes: A Self-Verifying Agent Instrument that Dissociates Commitment Drift from Binding Drift in Long-Horizon Agents
articles.summary: arXiv:2608.04066v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: How do you verify a long-horizon agent when its own state and self-reports are exactly what you cannot trust? We present an agent instrument built so that verification is structural rather than post-hoc. A deterministic Executive owns all belief; a language model may only file typed proposals, and a claim is admitted only when a prediction pre-registered before acting is matched against observation by code. articles.title: Monte Carlo Tree Search for Table-to-Multimodal Report Generation
articles.summary: arXiv:2608.04071v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Automatically generating professional multimodal reports comprising both textual analysis and visual charts from structured tabular data is a critical challenge in data intelligence. Existing methods suffer from fixed linear pipelines and isolated subtask processing, which hinder joint optimization of factual accuracy, visual quality, and narrative coherence. articles.title: FinProBench: Evaluating Financial AI Agents with Role-Grounded Rubrics Derived from Professional Deliverables
articles.summary: arXiv:2608.04077v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Evaluating financial AI agents requires criteria aligned with real professional work. Existing rubric methods typically derive criteria from task prompts or model outputs, overlooking tacit standards visible only in practitioner deliverables. We introduce FinProBench, a benchmark for professional financial tasks, and Role-Grounded Rubric Construction (RGRC), a reusable pipeline that derives rubrics from deliverables produced by practitioners in the same role. RGRC comprises four stages: Deliverable Collection, Competency Extraction, Rubric Synthe

articles.summary: arXiv:2608.04013v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Recent advances in Multimodal Emotion Recognition in Conversations (MERC) highlight its reliance on complete multimodal inputs. articles.title: Gratitude makes people more helpful, but it doesn’t overcome the bystander effect
articles.summary: A new study published in Cognition and Emotion indicates that while gratitude boosts your overall willingness to help someone in need, it doesn't overcome the bystander effect. Even grateful people hesitate when a crowd is present.

articles.title: Psychological distress isolates men more than women, according to a 14-year study
articles.summary: Social support boosts mental health for both sexes, but a new study shows men face a unique trap. When experiencing psychological distress, men are far more likely than women to withdraw and lose their social safety nets.

articles.summary: arXiv:2608.04218v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Whenever we look at an object, we seem to perceive it immediately. However, this is not the case for two reasons. articles.title: THC medication made PTSD nightmares disappear for more than a third of patients
articles.summary: A prescription form of THC helped many people with PTSD escape recurring trauma-related nightmares, with more than one-third reporting that the nightmares disappeared completely after ten weeks. The results could point toward a long-awaited treatment for one of PTSD’s most distressing and stubborn symptoms.

articles.title: Nearly half of dementia cases may be linked to risks you can change
articles.summary: A long-term brain study found that common risks such as smoking, high blood pressure, heart disease, and high blood lipids were strongly linked to damage associated with vascular dementia. The findings suggest that healthier lifestyle choices could help delay dementia by reducing several harmful brain changes at once.

articles.title: Brief DMT trips linked to lasting improvements in quality of life for depressed patients
articles.summary: A new study indicates that brief experiences with inhaled DMT can reduce anxiety and improve life satisfaction. For patients with treatment-resistant depression, the substance combined with therapy might promote long-lasting enhancements in overall quality of life.

articles.title: Animal studies suggest that reproductive behavior fully recovers after puberty-blocking treatment ends
articles.summary: Temporarily pausing puberty with leuprolide in adolescent rats delays reproductive development. However, research in Biology of Sex Differences and Hormones and Behavior provides evidence that subjects achieve full physical and behavioral maturation after treatment ends.
